content: TLV (type-length-value) encoding is the standard technique for versioned/extensible binary structs: each optional field is tagged with a type id and length prefix so unknown-to-the-reader tags can be skipped by advancing length bytes rather than failing to parse. A schema-version field checked first, then conditional field reads, is the standard C++ pattern; fixed-length base fields are kept for parse efficiency, with TLV reserved for the genuinely optional/extension region.
